content.overview: The Board may constitute such number of committees as it may deem fit to assist it in the efficient discharge of its functions, but shall not delegate any of its powers or assign the powers of the Chief Executive to any committee. A committee may, with Board approval, co-opt members, provided the Chief Executive or a director is a member. Every committee functions under the general superintendence, direction and control of the Board. Fees and allowances are fixed by the Board. Minutes of each committee meeting must be placed before the Board at its next meeting.
content.glance: Board may form committees to assist it; no delegation of Board or Chief Executive powers; Chief Executive or a director must be a member; minutes go to the next Board meeting.
content.study: Section 378U enables the Board to constitute committees for assistance while preserving Board control. The Board cannot delegate its own powers or the Chief Executive’s powers to a committee. Co-option is allowed with Board approval, but the Chief Executive or a director must sit on the committee. Committees work under Board superintendence, and their minutes must be reported to the next Board meeting.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Board may constitute committees to assist it, without delegating Board or Chief Executive powers; the Chief Executive or a director must be a member; minutes go to the next Board meeting.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378U
examples.body: The Board constitutes a finance committee that includes the Chief Executive; the committee’s minutes are placed before the next Board meeting.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378U?
hypotheticals.analysis: It allows Board committees for assistance while barring delegation of Board or Chief Executive powers and requiring Board reporting.

rows.right: Board meetings and quorum (s. 378V) or Chief Executive (s. 378W)

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a committee may exercise the Board’s residual powers.
misconceptions.correction: s. 378U prohibits delegation of Board powers or of the Chief Executive’s powers to a committee.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378U be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm committee constitution for assistance. II. Check no improper delegation. III. Confirm membership and minutes reporting.

revisionPoints: Committee of directors — assist only; no Board/CE power delegation; CE or director member; minutes to Board
